equivalent.label: checkContinue: Node sends 100 Continue itself, also for a request that never runs
equivalent.reason: without the listener Node writes the interim 100 Continue itself when the response is assigned the socket (a queued response buffers it, a dropped one never sends it) and then calls the same listener: the lane already starts the requests one at a time, so no client can tell the two orders apart; the listener only makes the moment explicit

equivalent.label: decide() on a parse error: the requests waiting behind the one in flight still start
equivalent.reason: mechanism, not a proof of every state: the lane advances only when the first response closes, which after a parse error is the destroy of the socket; a handler that then starts on a destroyed socket has no remoteAddress and refuses at its first check (LOCAL_HOST_REQUIRED) without an effect and without an answer, so the queue drop only removes that dependency; no public observation tells the two apart

equivalent.label: ONLY the socket destroy after the flush
equivalent.reason: Node itself destroys the socket (destroySoon on 'finish') after a response that says Connection: close, at the same moment: the explicit destroy only makes the closing independent of that Node behaviour, and no suite (the flood test included) can tell the two apart; the pipelining guard is the mark, not the destroy
